unmapped_findings: Formation enthalpy ΔH_f = -0.391 eV·atom^-1 and cohesive energy E_coh = -6.947 eV·atom^-1 (Table 1, [b0021]); FeAl has the lowest formation enthalpy, hence is the most thermodynamically stable alloy in the Fe1-xMnxAl system ([b0022],[b0078]).

Elastic constants (Table 2, [b0049]): C11 = 294.0 GPa, C12 = 133.7 GPa, C44 = 157.0 GPa. FeAl has the highest C11 (294.0 GPa), indicating high incompressibility under uniaxial stress along x, and the largest C44 (157.0 GPa) ([b0042],[b0044]).
Bulk modulus B = 187.1 GPa and shear modulus G = 119.8 GPa (Table 2, [b0049]); both are the highest in the Fe1-xMnxAl series ([b0044]).
Poisson's ratio σ = 0.236 and B/G = 1.56 (Table 2, [b0049]); since B/G < 1.75, FeAl is classified as brittle ([b0045]).

Anisotropy indices (Table 3, [b0051]): A^U = 0.56 (smallest → most elastically isotropic in the series), A_B = 0, A_G = 0.053, A_1 = A_2 = A_3 = 1.96 (weakest shear-modulus anisotropy in (100)/(010)/(001) planes) ([b0059],[b0063]).

Electron density maps (Fig. 4, [figure_004]): FeAl-(011) total electron density contour map with Slice 1 colour bar 0.075–0.750 and electron density difference map with colour bar −0.030 to 0.060; elongated contours along Al–Fe bond axes indicate covalent interactions.
